A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same long-term fairness survey. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, references, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reviews published methods and findings. Table 1 classifies prior work, and the appendix contains search methodology and notation, without original empirical results.

after.justification: v3 remains a literature survey. Its additional application summaries and critical analysis discuss cited research without reporting original experiments, simulations, or empirical data analyses.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes an algorithm or model. v3 expands explanations and reviews additional methods, while retaining the survey's taxonomy.

E1.justification: Neither version conducts training or evaluation on datasets. The added admission-hiring discussion reviews prior work, while RLHF appears as a future direction.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates baselines against a proposed system. Table 1 retains the same surveyed methods; additional citations do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: No evaluation splits, metrics, training budgets, or testing procedures change. The expanded modeling descriptions in Sections 2 and 6 concern conceptual frameworks.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity experiments, or empirical case analyses are introduced. The new Section 7 provides critical discussion of existing literature.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Confidence intervals mentioned in Section 4.1 remain components of a cited bandit algorithm.

E6.justification: v3 Section 7 newly reports Zezulka and Genin's finding that fairness constraints on risk predictions can undermine reductions in long-term unemployment and gender gaps. Section 5.2 also specifies minority network-size and utility disadvantages in Akpinar et al. These are additions or refinements to cited qualitative findings.

T1.justification: Definitions 1–9 and their equations, the MDP and bandit formulations, and optimization expressions are retained. Added conceptual discussion supplies no new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and stated contributions retain the taxonomy, review of long-term fairness methods, and identification of challenges. The expanded critique develops the critical-review objective already stated in v2.

C2.justification: New Section 7 substantially expands analysis of favorable decisions versus beneficial outcomes, policy dependence, fragmented fairness notions, latent causal factors, and limitations of empirical benchmarks. Sections 2, 3, 4, and 6 additionally clarify framework boundaries, taxonomy non-exhaustiveness, and strategic-adaptation limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 retains the same seed papers, keywords, venues, and citation-tracking strategy. Neither version supplies implementation specifications or code/data access instructions that change in v3.

R1.justification: v3 substantially broadens connections to normative critiques, economic admission-hiring studies, strategic classification, provider max-min fairness, and latent causal discovery. Examples include Kannan et al. (2019), Estornell et al. (2023), and Xu et al. (2023a); the retained ELBERT reference becomes Xu et al. (2023b).

P1.justification: Most prose and the existing section sequence remain. v3 inserts a critical-analysis section, expands selected explanations, corrects grammar and cross-references, and adds acknowledgments and affiliation/publication information.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 and Tables 1–2 retain their graphics and structure. Journal headers and text reflow alter placement: Table 1 appears within Section 4.1, and Table 2 follows methodology text instead of occupying a separate appendix page.

improvement.justification: Clearer framework boundaries in Sections 2 and 6 and the new Section 7 improve guidance on welfare assumptions, policy dependence, and practical limitations. These additions deepen the critical discussions already present in v2 and make the retained taxonomy more useful, supporting a limited overall quality improvement.
